## Critique
- claim-1: The bounded target is established by artifact `11083cba2a0e58c0f6806d6dbca8cb2df9600abf8e2fb2d94fd0ad46ec5ea0f7` (exit status \(0\)). For every \(4\le d\le16\), it records the ordered columns, prescribed \(B_d\), complementary indices \(D_d\), complete labelled Pieri rows, one-based \(P_d\), \(U_d=M_d[P_d,D_d]\), and \(\det U_d=\pm1\). It verifies every nonselected-row residual
  \[
  M_d[r,B_d]-M_d[r,D_d]U_d^{-1}M_d[P_d,B_d]
  \]
  is the zero vector, including empty vectors when \(B_d=\varnothing\). The degree-\(4\) witness is explicitly \(M_4=0_{0\times1}\), \(D_4=0_{0\times0}\), \(P_4=\varnothing\), \(U_4=I_0\), \(\det U_4=1\). The script invokes no Smith routine. Unimodularity and the residual identities show that the selected rows generate the complete row lattice; after ordering columns as \(D_d,B_d\), this lattice is the graph of an integral map over \(\mathbb Z^{D_d}\). Hence the Smith data consist of \(|D_d|\) unit entries and \(|B_d|\) zero entries, exactly as reported. The notation is reconciled by lower shape \(22\), upper box \(4^4\), with \(i=j=p=c=2\).
- claim-2: Correctly limits the result to this finite \([22,4^4]\), degree-\(4\) through degree-\(16\) certificate. It establishes neither an all-parameter algorithm nor the broader parent theorem.
